ending_skeptic_distrust.text: The beam passes over the north rocks. For a moment the fog brightens where Edith said the other light would be.

ending_skeptic_distrust_2.text: You wait through another turn. Water, glass, a tired pair of eyes. You have an explanation you can live with.

ending_skeptic_distrust_3.text: You close her ledger. In the new one, you record the weather and the condition of the lamp. Nothing about an answer.

ending_skeptic_distrust_epilogue.text: The radio stays quiet. You have told no one on the mainland what you found.

ending_skeptic_distrust_radioed_tom.text: The beam passes over the north rocks. For a moment the fog brightens where Edith said the other light would be.

ending_skeptic_distrust_radioed_tom_2.text: You wait through another turn. Water, glass, a tired pair of eyes. You have an explanation you can live with.

ending_skeptic_distrust_radioed_tom_3.text: You close her ledger. In the new one, you record the weather and the condition of the lamp. Nothing about an answer.

ending_skeptic_distrust_radioed_tom_epil.text: You remember Tom asking whether you were settling in. You have an ordinary answer ready for the next time he calls.

ending_skeptic_distrust_4.text: By morning, the light has kept its hours. You decide that is all it has ever done.

ending_skeptic_trust.text: You cannot make a signal out of what you saw beyond the rocks. But Edith's careful entries remain in front of you.

ending_skeptic_trust_2.text: You leave her pages intact. Beside tonight's date, you write: I saw the light she described. I do not know what she saw in it.

ending_skeptic_trust_3.text: There is work before dawn. Oil to measure, glass to clean. You keep the lamp burning for whoever might need the way back.

ending_skeptic_trust_epilogue.text: You leave the ledger beside the radio. You have not yet spoken to Tom; for now, the account has only you to keep it.

ending_skeptic_trust_radioed_tom.text: You cannot make a signal out of what you saw beyond the rocks. But Edith's careful entries remain in front of you.

ending_skeptic_trust_radioed_tom_2.text: You leave her pages intact. Beside tonight's date, you write: I saw the light she described. I do not know what she saw in it.

ending_skeptic_trust_radioed_tom_3.text: There is work before dawn. Oil to measure, glass to clean. You keep the lamp burning for whoever might need the way back.

ending_skeptic_trust_radioed_tom_epilogu.text: Tom asked you to bring what you found to him first. You leave the ledger beside the radio, ready for that conversation.

ending_skeptic_trust_4.text: The beam turns. You watch the water until it comes around again.

ending_believer_trust.text: Three flashes beyond the north rocks. Then darkness. You no longer count them to find the mistake.

ending_believer_trust_2.text: You open Edith's ledger to the place where her writing narrows. Under her last account, you add your own.

ending_believer_trust_3.text: She did not invent the answering light. Whatever took her out onto the water, you will not let that part of her story disappear.

ending_believer_trust_epilogue.text: You have not called the mainland. Edith's words and your own lie together on the page, still unread by anyone else.

ending_believer_trust_radioed_tom.text: Three flashes beyond the north rocks. Then darkness. You no longer count them to find the mistake.

ending_believer_trust_radioed_tom_2.text: You open Edith's ledger to the place where her writing narrows. Under her last account, you add your own.

ending_believer_trust_radioed_tom_3.text: She did not invent the answering light. Whatever took her out onto the water, you will not let that part of her story disappear.

ending_believer_trust_radioed_tom_epilog.text: You remember Tom's voice coming through the static. When you tell someone what you saw, you will not have to begin with a stranger.

ending_believer_trust_4.text: You keep the rhythm. When the distant light answers, hers is the name you say.

ending_believer_distrust.text: The light beyond the north rocks answers again. You believe it now. That does not mean you believe it wanted to be found.

ending_believer_distrust_2.text: Edith wrote as though a reply were an invitation. You read the words once more, then close the book.

ending_believer_distrust_3.text: You tend the lamp and keep its ordinary sweep across the water. You send no private rhythm into the fog.

ending_believer_distrust_epilogue.text: You have not spoken to Tom. Between turns of the beam, the radio sits within reach.

ending_believer_distrust_radioed_tom.text: The light beyond the north rocks answers again. You believe it now. That does not mean you believe it wanted to be found.

ending_believer_distrust_radioed_tom_2.text: Edith wrote as though a reply were an invitation. You read the words once more, then close the book.

ending_believer_distrust_radioed_tom_3.text: You tend the lamp and keep its ordinary sweep across the water. You send no private rhythm into the fog.

ending_believer_distrust_radioed_tom_epi.text: You remember Tom telling you to keep the light steady. His voice is easy to recall in the pauses between the flashes.

ending_believer_distrust_4.text: Out past the rocks, three flashes come without yours. You stay beside the lamp.
